title: Pre-Analysis — Extension of the Cabin-Flex Rear Galley and Deep Stowage Arrangement to a Further Conversion Population
abstract: Pre-analysis of a request to offer the rear galley complex and deep stowage arrangement as a retrofit conversion to a second operator, covering the weight and balance envelope, the conversion slot and the published cabin content.

sections.objective: Determine what has to change for the rear galley and deep stowage arrangement, released as a production and single-customer retrofit standard, to be offered as a general conversion. The question is less about the design than about what else the aircraft has to be at when the conversion is done: which service systems in the same aft section are affected, which retrofit slots the conversion competes with, and whether the published cabin content can carry a third rear-end configuration without becoming unreadable.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and one of them attaches a condition. The conversion bulletin as issued is written around one customer's monument layout and carries the part numbers of that layout in its material list; offering the arrangement generally means re-issuing it with a configurable material list rather than extending its effectivity. The second item came out of the semantic pass rather than the entity pass: the long-sector water capacity increase changes the aft service load in the same section, and although the two share no part number, no zone and no drawing, an aircraft that has both sits noticeably further aft than either change was substantiated against. The third item is a scheduling one. The door surround reinforcement on the same aircraft type needs the aft cargo compartment open, and the two are naturally done in one visit; done separately they cost the operator a second downtime.
sections.next_steps: Re-issue the conversion bulletin with a configurable monument material list instead of extending the current effectivity. Ask weight and balance to run the combined case with the increased water capacity and publish the result as a loading condition rather than leaving it to the operator. Offer the conversion and the door surround reinforcement as a paired downtime package and confirm the combined ground time with the conversion centre before quoting it.

similarity_seeds: rear galley complex and stowage volume on a long sector single aisle
aft service load and centre of gravity on a converted cabin
conversion downtime shared with an aft cargo compartment task

tasks.title: Search released cabin modifications acting on the aft monument area
Review the conversion bulletin material list for customer-specific items
Assess the combined aft loading case with other released aft changes
Confirm the downtime overlap with structural retrofit work on the same type

expected_findings.rationale: The conversion bulletin material list is written for one customer's monument layout. Extending its effectivity to a second operator would call up monuments that operator does not have and omit the ones it does.
expected_findings.resolution: Re-issue the bulletin with a configurable monument material list keyed to the delivered cabin standard.

evidence.similarity_note: Both changes add mass and service capability to the same aft section of a long-sector ZEPHYR-24 and are described in completely different vocabulary — 'deep stowage and rear galley complex' against 'potable water capacity increase for long-sector operations'. They share no part number, no functional item number, no zone and no drawing; only the descriptive text and the operational rationale connect them.

expected_findings.rationale: An aircraft carrying both changes sits further aft than either was substantiated against. Neither dossier considered the other because the two sit in different chapters and were raised eight years apart.
expected_findings.resolution: Run the combined weight and balance case and publish the result as a loading condition in the conversion bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The door surround reinforcement applies to exactly the same aircraft type and requires the aft cargo compartment to be opened. The conversion needs the same access for the rear monument removal, so performing them separately buys the operator a second downtime for no engineering reason.
expected_findings.resolution: Offer the two as a paired downtime package and agree the combined ground time with the conversion centre.

expected_non_findings.reason: Returned high by the semantic pass because it also changes the aft fuselage interior on the same aircraft type and uses similar installation language, but it fits thermo-acoustic blankets above the cargo compartment ceiling. It shares no zone, no part number and no monument with the galley arrangement and is embodied from below the cabin floor.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with a positive position subject to two conditions: a configurable material list in the re-issued bulletin, and a published combined loading condition for aircraft that also carry the increased water capacity.
